stories.title: Israel expanding presence in Lebanon, officials say, as BBC visits occupied areas
stories.summary: The drive on the highway by the Mediterranean in southern Lebanon, near the border with Israel, is scenic and, these days, desolate. Crops lie abandoned and buildings destroyed by Israeli air strikes, too many to count, are in ruins. Near the town of Naqoura, a Lebanese military checkpoint, painted in the white-and-red colours of the national flag, is the last visible sign of the state's presence. Soldiers are positioned behind concrete walls, but the road is empty. A few minutes further south, around a dozen Israeli flags indicate the start of occupied territory. Unless authorised by Israel, no-one can enter. This part of the country is the heartland of Lebanon's Shia Muslim community, from which Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed militia and political party, gets most of its support. It has seen three invasions by the Israeli military in wars against the group in the last two decades alone. The most recent started in March, after Hezbollah fired rockets into Israel following the killing of the Iranian supreme leader, at the start of the US and Israel's war against Iran. Last month, a BBC team joined a humanitarian mission of the UN peacekeeping force in Lebanon, known as Unifil, which is one of the only ways to visit the area under Israeli control. There, as it did in Gaza, Israel has flattened entire villages, and air strikes and demolitions have continued even after a ceasefire was announced in June. Led by Finnish troops who are part of Unifil, the convoy was escorting civilians to and from Christian villages near the border.

stories.title: Footage shows Israeli destruction in south Lebanon's Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: Footage shows Israeli destruction in south Lebanon's Bint Jbeil A video circulating online shows massive and widespread destruction of the historic town of Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon. Repeated Israeli air strikes and attacks have left entire neighbourhoods, homes, and local infrastructure heavily damaged or completely reduced to rubble. stories.title: Two Turkish-flagged commercial vessels collide off Istanbul, governor's office says
stories.summary: ISTANBUL, Sept 2 - Two Turkish-flagged commercial vessels collided off Istanbul in the Sea of Marmara on Wednesday and contact has been lost with one of the ships, the Istanbul governor's office said.
article_sentences: Two Turkish-flagged commercial vessels collided off Istanbul in the Sea of Marmara on Wednesday and contact has been lost with one of the ships, the Istanbul governor's office said.

The Turkish-flagged Alsu, en route to the Aegean port of Aliaga, and the Turkish-flagged Tugberk Imamoglu, en route to the Black Sea port of Karadenizeregli, collided off the Silivri district of Istanbul at around 3 a.m. (0000 GMT) on Wednesday, the governor's office said in a statement.
Coast guard ships and helicopters were dispatched to the scene for search and rescue, and there was no visible damage on the Alsu, the statement said.
But authorities were unable to establish contact with the Tugberk Imamoglu and its 10 crew members.

According to data from the Istanbul Chamber of Maritime Commerce, the Tugberk Imamoglu, owned by Zeybe Denizcilik, operates as a bulk carrier, while the Alsu, owned by Ozpulathane Deniz Tasimaciligi, operates as a chemical tanker.

stories.headline: CityU vows ‘zero tolerance’ as orientation ‘disco night’ video triggers probe

opening: Hong Kong’s City University has launched an investigation into an alleged indecent incident during a student-led orientation activity after a video surfaced showing a half-naked man carrying a woman wearing only a bra and shorts.

The university issued a statement on Wednesday pledging “zero tolerance” for improper conduct, after a social media clip appeared to show intimate behaviour among individuals believed to be students during what the video caption described as a “disco night”.
